From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + suggested eval plan (Acme rerank)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for a productive call today — appreciate the time walking through your current search funnel and where reranking could move the needle. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Problem: navigation + search results quality drop for long-tail queries; click-through and conversion delta on page 2 is significant.
- What we propose: run a focused reranking evaluation using your historical query->click labels and our small candidate transformer reranker + lightweight BM25 baseline.

Suggested initial model candidates (to validate fit):
- redwood/rerank-tiny-2b (low-latency, quantization-friendly) — baseline candidate for throughput testing
- redwood/rerank-small-4b-q4 (recommended for NDCG lifts)
- open/rerank-encoder-1.5b (external benchmark)

Data & access we need from your side:
1) A sample of 10k labeled query sessions (query, candidates, click label, timestamp) — can be partial/anonymized.
2) A small holdout set (~2k) we should reserve for final validation/A-B.

I attached a short sample schema and a placeholder file you can drop data into (acme_eval_sample.jsonl). If you’re comfortable, please share upload link or S3 credentials; otherwise we can set up a short SFTP exchange.

Next steps / timeline:
- Alex: share sample data by Friday 7/3 if possible.
- Redwood: run first-pass eval (NDCG@10, MRR, latency per candidate) and send results within 5 business days of receiving data.
- Align on A/B plan & rollout window after initial validation.

Attachments: acme_eval_sample.jsonl (schema + stub)

Thanks — I’ll loop Michael in for the technical validation and he can include an early NDCG/MRR template we usually use.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference

Hi Alex / Priya — looping in some technical details so you know what to expect from our early validation run.

Thanks for the sample. We parsed the schema fine. A few notes on metrics and plan: 

- Metrics: we’ll report NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, and per-query latency (p50/p95) for each candidate model vs BM25 baseline.
- Significance: we’ll use paired bootstrap for confidence intervals and report p-values for NDCG lifts; practical threshold we typically flag is >1.5 NDCG@10 absolute lift or >5% relative MRR increase depending on query distribution.
- Baselines: BM25 (current control), rerank-tiny-2b (low-latency candidate), rerank-small-4b-q4 (our expected improvement candidate).
- Quality regression concerns: if we see regressions on head queries (high-traffic queries), we recommend a conservative canary with fallback.

I attached the first-pass results from a small internal simulation we ran on a mirrored toy dataset so you can preview the CSV format (acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.csv). Note these are synthetic but representative — actual numbers will change when we run on your production labels.

Proposed A/B plan (high-level):
1) Offline validation (this run) — 5 business days after data receipt.
2) Canary A/B (2 weeks, 5-10% traffic) — monitor NDCG and negative quality regression signals; auto-fallback on degradation.
3) Ramp (if canary successful) to 25% then 100% with automated rollbacks and shadow testing in parallel.

Open question: are you running any downstream re-ranking business rules (e.g., freshness boosts, manual pinning) that we should replicate in the offline scoring? If so, please share the rules so our offline eval matches online logic.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min tech sync if helpful.

—Michael
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
